findings.asked: Find the original value after an 18.2% decrease.
findings.wentWrong: Very few correct. Most found 18.2% of the given value and subtracted it. Those whose first line was 'given value = 81.8%' nearly always finished.
findings.rule: First line: the given value is (100 - 18.2)% of the original.

findings.asked: The same reverse-percentage question on M4.
findings.wentWrong: Mean mark two out of three; the same wrong start, taking the percentage of the final value, scored zero.
findings.rule: Never take a percentage of the final value in a reverse question.

findings.wentWrong: Well answered, but two zero-scoring starts recurred: 28% of the given value subtracted, or the given value equated to 72% instead of 128%. A few used the wrong number from the question.
findings.rule: An increase means the given value is more than 100% of the original.

findings.wentWrong: One of the poorest questions: few even equated the value to 90% for the first step; the usual approach was to add 10% on.
findings.rule: Reverse each change in turn, each time writing 'value = ...%'.

findings.wentWrong: About 37% full marks; most reversed only one of the two changes, or simply found 10% and subtracted then 15% and added.

findings.asked: A reverse percentage in an unusual wording, then a further step to the quantity asked.
findings.wentWrong: Pleasingly many found the original (24% = the difference, so 100% = 86), but then forgot to add the difference to reach the first-class fare, or subtracted it.
findings.rule: After the reverse step, re-read what quantity the question wants.

findings.wentWrong: Most correctly began with 112% = the given amount. The common slip afterwards was subtracting from the wrong value after increasing 900 by 17.6%; starting by finding 12% and subtracting scored nothing.
findings.rule: Keep track of which quantity each percentage refers to.

findings.wentWrong: Those who wrote 93.8% = given value usually finished; some set that up and then reverted to adding or subtracting 6.2%; others used 106.2% because 'depreciated' was not understood.
findings.rule: Depreciation is a decrease: the given value is below 100%.

findings.wentWrong: Most recognised it; those who did not either found 6.2% and subtracted or started from 106.2%.
findings.rule: Read the direction word before choosing the percentage.

ruleToRemember: Write '(100 plus or minus r)% = given value' as the first line, divide to get 1%, multiply to get 100%; decrease or depreciation means below 100%; then check which quantity the question actually asks for.
aStarSignal: Two reversals in a row, or a reversal buried in unusual wording, followed by a correct final step to the quantity requested.
